evaluation_construct.audience: Inferred ordinary, interested non-expert adult reader who encounters social influence in consumer, school, workplace, civic, or group settings.

evaluation_construct.purpose: Explain when visible social behavior carries useful information, when it instead reflects pressure or a misleading norm, and how to respond to or redesign the cue.
intended_outcomes: Distinguish informational social proof from approval, authority pressure, hidden dissent, and repetition.
Recognize when publicizing common bad behavior may reinforce it.
Use a diagnostic pause, dissent statement, stop line, or revised norm message in an appropriate situation.

verdict: As a standalone chapter, this is a clear, humane, and practically useful explanation of how visible social cues can inform, pressure, or mislead, with strong local mental-model and transfer support. Its 70.8 chapter diagnostic remains materially limited by missing quiz feedback, repetitive and partly unmapped components, lightly qualified evidence, and weak implementation follow-through; no full-book score or certification can be inferred.
